stem:
The diagram shows an object released from point X and travelling on a frictionless track. If a heavier object is taken in consideration then

(The figure shows a smooth, undulating frictionless track. Point X is at the top of the first hill at height 25 m, point Y on the same hill is at 15 m, the track dips to the lowest point Z on the ground, then rises to a second peak M at 20 m and falls to point N at 10 m.)

1. It will move with a greater speed at Y.
2. The speed of the object at M is 10 m s⁻¹.

options.label: A
options.text: Neither (i) nor (ii) is true.

options.label: B
options.text: Only (i) is true.

options.label: C
options.text: Both (i) and (ii) are true.

options.label: D
options.text: Only (ii) is true.

stem:
The diagram shows a cyclist moving down a small hill at P before travelling on a flat road after point Q. The total mass of the cyclist and his bicycle is 60 kg and the speed of the cyclist at P is 10 m s⁻¹. Which of the following is incorrect? (Take acceleration due to gravity, g = 10 m s⁻²)

(The figure shows a raised flat platform at height 3 m on the left with the cyclist at its right edge P; from P the surface curves smoothly downward to the lower flat road on the right, where point Q lies at the foot of the slope.)

options.label: A
options.text: The loss of gravitational energy between P and Q is 1800 J.

options.label: B
options.text: Total energy is 4800 J.

options.label: C
options.text: The cyclist does not require a greater power when he travels at a higher constant speed.

options.label: D
options.text: The kinetic energy at P is 3000 J.

stem:
Two inclined frictionless tracks, one gradual and the other steep meet at point A from where two stones (I and II) are allowed to slide down from rest, one on each track as shown in figure. Which of the following statements is correct?

(The figure shows a triangle with apex A at height h. The left side is a long, gentle incline down to point B on the ground along which stone I slides; the right side is a short, steep incline down to point C on the ground along which stone II slides. Both stones start from rest at A.)

options.label: A
options.text: Both the stones reach the bottom at the same time but not with the same speed.

options.label: B
options.text: Both the stones reach the bottom with the same speed and stone II reaches the bottom earlier than stone I.

options.label: C
options.text: Both the stones reach the bottom at different times and with different speeds.

options.label: D
options.text: Both the stones reach the bottom with the same speed and stone I reaches the bottom earlier than stone II.

stem:
A graph of the total energy of a freely falling body from a height is

(The four options are graphs of total energy T.E. on the vertical axis against height h on the horizontal axis.)

options.label: A
options.text: A curve that rises steeply from the origin and then bends over to level off (concave).

options.label: B
options.text: A horizontal straight line (total energy stays constant as h changes).

options.label: C
options.text: A straight line rising from the origin (total energy increases in proportion to h).

options.label: D
options.text: A straight line falling from a high value down to the h-axis (total energy decreases as h increases).

stem:
A skier of mass 50 kg stands at point P at the top of the ski jump and moves from P to Q and takes off his jump at Q as shown in figure. If 50% of the change in the gravitational potential energy of the skier between points P and Q becomes the kinetic energy at Q, then the speed at which the skier arrives at Q is

(The figure shows a valley-shaped ski run above the ground: P is at the top of the left side at height 60 m, the track dips down through the valley and rises to the take-off point Q on the right at height 20 m.)

options.label: A
options.text: 10 m s⁻¹

options.label: B
options.text: 20 m s⁻¹

options.label: C
options.text: 40 m s⁻¹

options.label: D
options.text: 30 m s⁻¹

stem:
A box of 5 kg mass moves up a ramp from point A to point B at a constant speed. Given that the surfaces are smooth (frictionless). What is the gain in the potential energy by the box? (g = 10 m s⁻²)

(The figure shows the box starting at A on the ground. From A a straight inclined ramp of length 10 m rises to a height of 8 m, with a horizontal base of 6 m, forming a 6-8-10 right triangle. From the top of the ramp a horizontal stretch of 10 m runs across to point B at the same height.)

A body moves under a variable force. For the body a plot of velocity versus time is shown in figure. The correct statement is

(The figure shows a velocity-time graph. From O the velocity rises in a straight line up to A, stays constant along the horizontal segment A to B, then falls in a straight line to C where it crosses the time axis to zero, and continues falling below the axis to D where the velocity is negative.)

options.label: A
options.text: In moving from B to C, work done by the force on the body is positive

options.label: B
options.text: In moving from A to B, the body does work on the system

options.label: C
options.text: In moving from O to A, work done by the force on the body is negative

options.label: D
options.text: In moving from C to D, work done by the force on the body is positive
